title: Tea Reached Tibet Only by Horseback — China's Tea-Horse Road | China Travel Expert
description:
For more than a thousand years, before any road or railway, tea reached Tibet the hard way — on the backs of horses and mules.

The Tea-Horse Road (茶马古道) was a network of caravan trails winding through the mountains of Yunnan toward Tibet, in use from the Tang dynasty until the 20th century. Tibet couldn't grow tea but couldn't live without it, so caravans hauled compressed tea bricks over passes above 4,500 metres, trading them for horses along the way. Of all its towns, Shaxi in Yunnan is the only complete caravan stop still standing — a real window onto the route.

🧭 Expert Tip: Base yourself in Shaxi rather than Lijiang. It's the last intact Tea-Horse Road market town, far quieter than the big old towns, and the Friday market still fills the old square.

一千年里，茶叶是靠马帮翻山越岭，一路驮到西藏的。
